facts.claim: AYANA Bali hosts weddings: its official weddings page describes an expert wedding team and dedicated planners who guide couples through details such as cake and florals, working with the resort's chefs and restaurants.

AYANA Bali lists outdoor wedding venues with stated capacities: Champa Garden (ceremony 800 / reception 3000), SKY, described as an open stage overlooking the sea and sky (ceremony 80 / reception 300), AYANA Villa, described with panoramic 180-degree views of the Indian Ocean (ceremony 80 / reception 350).

AYANA Bali lists further outdoor venues: KISIK Pier, described as a ceremony bathed in the glow of a sunset (ceremony 30 / reception 80); Asmara Gazebo, a gazebo from the Javanese royal palace (ceremony 50 / reception 70); Bale Kencana, with stone pathways and a traditional Balinese split gate (ceremony 30 / reception 50); Rock Bar, described as exchanging vows privately above the ocean (reception 20, no ceremony figure).

AYANA Bali lists indoor wedding venues: Tresna Chapel, described as a white chapel that rises above the Indian Ocean (ceremony 70 / reception 50); Astina Pavilion, a glass-walled venue with 180-degree Indian Ocean views (ceremony 40); Orchid, a garden and glass greenhouse (ceremony 22 / reception 40); Amara Ballroom (ceremony 390 / reception 200 to 600); RIMBA Ballroom (ceremony 200 / reception 400).

AYANA Bali names four wedding packages on its weddings page: AYANA Villa Wedding, SKY is the Limit, Sweet Escape at KISIK Pier, and Tresna dream wedding by the cliff. It also lists spa treatments for the couple, music and entertainment, and themed wedding cakes.
AYANA Bali's own wedding venue list states ceremony and reception capacities separately for each space, from Rock Bar (reception 20) to Champa Garden (reception 3000).
Jumeirah Bali, on the brand's official site, describes itself as a wedding destination set against the backdrop of Dreamland Beach, overlooking Dreamland Beach on Bali's southern coast in Uluwatu.

Jumeirah Bali describes its resort as a Javanese-Hindu water palace-inspired haven with spacious villas and private pools for guests, and invites couples to speak to its luxury wedding experts to create a wedding package.

Jumeirah Bali's official wedding story features a couple who held their ceremony at the resort's fountain and their reception at Akasa, with villa categories named as Ocean Villa (2-bedroom), Panoramic Ocean Villa, Garden Villas and Sunset Villas. These are the couple's words on the brand's page, not a published venue specification.
Bvlgari Resort Bali's official weddings page lists wedding options named The Bvlgari Mansion Wedding, La Terrazza Wedding, The Bvlgari Chapel Wedding and The Bvlgari Villa Wedding, plus Celebrations.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Australian Embassy Indonesia 'Marriage in Indonesia' page: DFAT and its missions cannot advise on other countries' specific marriage requirements; contact the nearest Indonesian Embassy/Consulate-General or the Indonesian Civil Registry Office (Catatan Sipil) where the marriage will take place. The page is 'a general guide only'.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: generally persons of any nationality may marry in Indonesia provided they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government (page lists Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian); marriages may be performed by ministers of religion, Civil Registry Office officers or the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA); for a marriage to be legal it must be conducted according to the religion and conform to the laws of the countries of the parties.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page, heading 'Couples must be of the same religion': under Indonesian Law No. 1 of 1974 concerning marriage, both parties must hold the same religion; if not, one party must convert.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: an Australian citizen marrying in Indonesia needs a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) from the Australian Embassy Jakarta or the Consulates-General in Denpasar (Bali), Surabaya or Makassar. The Consulate-General Bali covers Bali, NTB and NTT. CNI usually issued while you wait if documents are complete; no expiry is set, but local Civil Registry Offices do not normally accept CNIs issued more than 3 months prior. You cannot marry at the Embassy/Consulate-General. No fee is stated on this page.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy page: Muslim weddings are performed by the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), which issues the Marriage Book (Buku Nikah); civil registration is usually not required but a Civil Registry marriage certificate is recommended if relocating. Non-Muslim marriages (Christian, Hindu, etc.): lodge a Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before the wedding, and after the ceremony the marriage must be registered at the Civil Registry Office to be legal. Documents: CNI, passports, birth certificates, proof of dissolution of a previous marriage or death certificate (if applicable), four 4x6 cm photos; requirements vary by province.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Embassy FAQ: since 1 January 1995 a marriage legally performed overseas that would have been legal in Australia is accepted as legal under Australian law; you do not register it with the Embassy and cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia.

[Copied from indonesian-wedding-traditions 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (updated 18/08/2026): you can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is recognised if valid where it happened and valid under Australian law had it occurred here; Australia doesn't recognise overseas marriages where a party is already married, underage, too closely related or forced. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country; ask the destination's embassy whether it needs authentication or apostille. Talk to a lawyer to confirm validity.

Smartraveller Indonesia (updated 21 October 2026, still current at 18 November 2026): overall advice 'Exercise a high degree of caution'; 'Reconsider your need to travel' applies only to the provinces of Papua Pegunungan and Papua Tengah. Bali is not named in a higher-level area, so the overall level applies to Bali.

Smartraveller Indonesia: before arriving at international entry points (plane or boat) travellers need to complete an arrival card and apply for an e-Visa on Arrival (e-VOA), both on the All Indonesia website. For a regular VOA, an ordinary passport needs at least 6 months validity from the planned entry date (6 months from departure also recommended) plus a return or onward flight booking. The e-VOA and VOA allow a 30-day stay, extendable once for up to 30 days at an immigration office. Damaged passports (including water damage or minor tears) have led to refused entry.

Smartraveller Indonesia: foreign tourists entering Bali must pay a tourist levy, separate from the e-VOA or VOA; cashless payment online before travel or at designated counters at Bali's airport and seaport. (Amount not recorded here; see the Bali Provincial Government site.)

Smartraveller Indonesia: volcanic activity may escalate with little or no notice, causing flight delays, cancellations or airport closures, including in surrounding provinces; Mount Agung in Bali Province is listed among volcanoes to watch, and trekking routes on or near Mount Agung and Mount Batur are named. Indonesia uses a 4-level volcano alert system (Normal, Advisory, Watch, Warning). Contact your airline for the latest flight information.

Smartraveller Indonesia: Indonesia is in an active earthquake region with a high level of earthquake activity that sometimes triggers tsunamis; high wave events can happen in coastal regions. Know the emergency plans at your accommodation. Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches including in Bali.

Smartraveller Indonesia: drinks may be spiked or contain methanol; there have been cases of methanol poisoning, including in Bali and Lombok; as little as one shot can be fatal; only drink branded alcohol. The legal drinking age is 21 (alcohol illegal in Aceh).

Smartraveller Indonesia: rabies is throughout Indonesia and 100% fatal once symptoms develop; get vaccinated before travel, avoid contact with dogs, cats, monkeys and bats, and get urgent care if bitten or scratched; rabies treatment may be limited. Dengue occurs including in Bali, and periodic measles outbreaks are reported including in Bali.

Smartraveller Indonesia: weather can change quickly during the wet season (usually around October to April; it can differ in Eastern Indonesia). Heavy rains can cause significant flooding in urban areas including Bali, disrupting roads and transport. No temperature or rainfall figures are given.

Smartraveller Indonesia: for consular help contact the Australian Embassy Jakarta or the Australian Consulates-General in Bali, Makassar or Surabaya. Emergency numbers: fire 113, ambulance and rescue 118, medical 119, police 110 or 112.

Australian Consulate-General Bali covers Bali, Nusa Tenggara Barat and Nusa Tenggara Timur; open Monday to Friday 8am to 4pm; consular, notarial and passport services are by appointment only, with security screening; payment by card only. After hours emergencies: call (+62 361) 2000 100 (press 4, then 6) for the 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre in Canberra, or (+61 2) 6261 3305.

Capella Ubud, Bali lists 'Ballroom' as the preferred venue option on its official wedding enquiry form; no other ceremony spaces, capacities or wedding service details are published on that page.
Capella Ubud, Bali gives its address as Jl. Raya Dalem, Banjar Triwangsa, Desa Keliki, Kecamatan Tegallalang, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali.
Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve describes its setting as 'rolling hills, a gentle river and verdant rice paddies' and offers bridal preparations, ceremony and reception at its Ubud venues.

Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve lists ceremony venues Temple Lawn (maximum 100 seated), Ayung Riverside/Kubu Riverside (maximum 100 seated), In-Villa Wedding (maximum 10 seated) and Rice Terrace Deck (maximum 30).
Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve states the Temple Lawn ceremony backdrop is the hundred-year-old Pengiyasan Temple, which stood before the resort was built.

Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve lists reception venues Temple Lawn (maximum 100 seated), Rice Terrace Deck (maximum 30 seated), and the Pool Bar and Library (maximum 30 each), plus Dining Beyond for two.
Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve names Marriott Certified Wedding Planners and dedicated Wedding Planners, and offers a dedicated personal assistant for the couple.
Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve states wedding packages include a non-legal wedding celebrant, and that its three-bedroom pool villas can host bridal preparations, ceremony and cocktail reception.
The Oberoi, Bali describes itself as offering stunning beachfront venues for destination weddings, with al fresco seaside, garden and poolside venues.
The Oberoi, Bali lists Serenity by the Sea, an open garden 'intimate Bali wedding venue' with ocean vistas, capacity 50 guests.
The Oberoi, Bali lists Bale Banjar, 112 square metres, with up to 50 guests for a standing cocktail and 24 to 32 at round tables.
Alila Seminyak describes itself as a beachfront resort on Bali's southwest coast, steps from the Indian Ocean, at the quieter end of the beach stretching north from Kuta and Legian.
Alila Seminyak states couples can exchange vows overlooking the Indian Ocean in customisable spaces, with a celebration tailor-made for them.
Alila Seminyak states its indoor venues, open-air terraces and event lawns can accommodate up to 250 guests (stated under Gatherings).
Alila Seminyak has its own Segara Temple on the resort and is near Pura Petitenget.
COMO Canggu (formerly COMO Uma Canggu) describes itself as 'the perfect destination for free-spirited weddings on Bali's sun-kissed southern coast', from a weekend for two to a resort buy-out.
COMO Canggu lists two wedding venues: COMO Beach Club (deck and lawn up to 50 seated each, dining area 100) and COMO Penthouse (40 total, private rooftop pool).
COMO Canggu states it hosts up to 80 guests for a resort buy-out and offers planning assistance, styling and entertainment services on request.
COMO Canggu states it is 60 minutes from Ngurah Rai International Airport.
The edge Bali presents The Sea Wedding as one of its wedding packages, with a stated wedding capacity of up to 50 guests.
The edge Bali's Sea Wedding places the ceremony at The villa and the reception at The venue, with a seated dinner or standing cocktail set-up for up to 50 guests.
The edge Bali's Sea Wedding includes a stay in a 1-bedroom villa (The villa) and a 5-bedroom villa (The view), with 24-hour butler service and airport and hotel transfers for in-house guests.
The edge Bali's Sea Wedding includes a celebrant blessing ceremony that the venue describes as non-legal, with a commemorative wedding certificate.
Renaissance Bali Uluwatu Resort & Spa states couples can say their vows in an enchanting chapel or on the beach, and describes its Bali outdoor wedding venues for ceremonies and receptions.
Renaissance Bali Uluwatu Resort & Spa offers personalised Uluwatu wedding packages, tailored catering and an expert team of planners, with a dedicated wedding expert contact.
Bvlgari Resort Bali describes itself as uniquely positioned atop a dramatic cliff with unrivalled views across the Indian Ocean.
Bvlgari Resort Bali states its beach and beachside restaurant are exclusive to in-house guests and reached only through the resort's inclined elevator; accommodation is in villas and mansions.
Samabe Bali Suites & Villas: its own events page invites couples to 'Plan Your Dream Wedding at Samabe Bali'.
Samabe Bali Suites & Villas describes itself as 'Your Private Cliffside Resort in Bali'.
Samabe Bali Suites & Villas offers exclusive buyouts: the entire resort reserved exclusively for your event, including two nights of accommodation for 260 guests.
Samabe Bali Suites & Villas says all resort employees are fully dedicated to the event during an exclusive buyout.

Samabe Bali Suites & Villas: its all-inclusive events package brings together catering, dedicated event coordination, audio-visual equipment and decor; it offers customisable event packages and can work with the couple's preferred vendors.
Samabe Bali Suites & Villas: site visits can be arranged by appointment; whether a minimum spend or rental fee applies depends on the venue and event type.

insider_details.detail: AYANA publishes ceremony and reception capacities separately for every space, so a 60-guest ceremony fits Tresna Chapel (70) but a seated reception for the same group needs another space (Tresna reception 50). Plan the ceremony-to-reception move as part of the timeline.

For intimate weddings at AYANA, KISIK Pier (ceremony 30), Bale Kencana (30) and Orchid (22) are sized for small groups, while Champa Garden and the ballrooms suit large celebrations on the same estate.

Jumeirah Bali positions its weddings around Dreamland Beach and its water-palace architecture; ask for the official venue list and capacities, as the brand's published wedding page is a couple story rather than a specification.

For a beach-and-banquet wedding over 200 guests at Four Seasons Jimbaran Bay, the beachfront Coconut Grove (reception 250) and Pool Terrace (reception 220) are the listed spaces; the private-island Gili Jimbaran caps at 100.
Mulia Bali prices and sizes by package; a package label is not a room capacity, so ask for a seating plan for the chapel before promising guest numbers.
Raffles Bali suits small weddings: the Presidential Villa takes 30 and the resort has 32 villas, so a full buyout of guest accommodation is a realistic question to ask.
Grand Hyatt Bali is the large-guest-list option in Nusa Dua, with a ballroom seating 736 for dinner as a wet-weather fallback to its garden and beach spaces.
Kempinski's Kimaya Chapel is indoor, air-conditioned and on an upper floor, a useful heat and rain plan for elopements and small ceremonies.
COMO Uma Ubud publishes the Yoga Studio as its wet weather option for Uma Bar events, so a poolside ceremony there has a named indoor fallback for up to 40 guests.
COMO Uma Ubud states the drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport is about 90 minutes, so build guest arrival transfers and a rest gap into the welcome-day timeline.
Four Seasons Sayan's aisle is a suspension bridge to the Rooftop Lotus Pond; plan for guests (and anyone with limited mobility) crossing a bridge to reach the ceremony.
At W Bali - Seminyak the beachfront venues (Starfish Bloo, Ice Garden, WET Deck) face the sunset, so time the ceremony and drinks around sunset and confirm the indoor Great Room as a rain plan.

Get the CNI from the Australian Consulate-General in Bali (by appointment) no more than 3 months before the wedding, and lodge the Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days ahead for a non-Muslim ceremony.
Ask every guest to check passport condition and 6 months validity, complete the arrival card and e-VOA online, and budget for the separate Bali tourist levy before flying.
Build a flight-disruption plan into the guest communication: volcanic activity can close airports at short notice, so couples should hold flexible bookings and an airline contact list.
Serve only branded, sealed spirits at the bar and brief guests on methanol risk; recommend guests speak to their doctor about rabies vaccination.
For weddings in the October to April wet season, plan a covered alternative and allow extra transfer time, as flooding can disrupt Bali roads.

At The St. Regis Bali Resort, the Cloud Nine Chapel seats only 30 (18 banquet), so a larger guest list either uses the beach or Amphitheatre for the ceremony, then moves to Cloud Nine Terrace (banquet 250) for dinner.

The St. Regis Bali Resort publishes a 7 PM limit for background music at the Amphitheatre, so plan garden ceremonies for late afternoon and move the party to another space for the evening; confirm music rules for the terrace at booking.
The St. Regis Bali Resort has an indoor fallback: the Astor Ballroom seats 150 banquet, useful as a rain plan for an outdoor terrace reception of up to 150.
For a welcome or rehearsal dinner for close family at The St. Regis Bali Resort, the Mezzanine of Kayuputi takes up to 20 guests.
Mandapa's ceremony spaces are small-to-mid scale (largest published 100 seated), so it suits intimate Ubud weddings rather than large guest lists.
Mandapa's packages use a non-legal celebrant, so couples should plan the legal marriage separately.
COMO Canggu's buy-out tops out at 80 guests and it is about an hour from the airport, so plan airport transfers as a group movement.
The edge Bali's Sea Wedding blessing is non-legal, so couples wanting a legally recognised marriage should plan the legal step separately.
